title: NTA UGC NET English Full Mock Test #13
subtitle: 100 Questions · 200 Marks · Post-2018 NTA Pattern · Zero Answer Bias (25 A/B/C/D) · Reading Comprehension (Q91-100)

items.title: Mock #13 · Q1
items.stem: Match List - I with List - II. List - I (Term) List - II (Coined by) (A) Heteroglossia (I) William Empson (B) Structures of Feeling (II) Raymond Williams (C) Ambiguity (III) Mikhail Bakhtin (D) Discourse (IV) Michel Foucault Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: The correct matches of theoretical concepts to their theorists are: Mikhail Bakhtin theorized 'heteroglossia' in 'Discourse in the Novel' [(A)-(III)]; Raymond Williams introduced 'structures of feeling' in The Long Revolution [(B)-(II)]; William Empson established 'ambiguity' in Seven Types of Ambiguity [(C)-(I)]; and Michel Foucault conceptualized 'discourse' in The Archaeology of Knowledge [(D)-(IV)].

items.title: Mock #13 · Q2
items.stem: Who has insisted that the power of the audience "derives from the fact that meanings do not circulate in the cultural economy in the same way that wealth does in the financial"?
items.explanation: In Television Culture (1987), media theorist John Fiske argues that the active audience's semiotic power derives from the fact that meanings circulate in the cultural economy differently from wealth in the financial economy.

items.title: Mock #13 · Q3
items.stem:
Which of these are generally taken to be true of Cultural Studies?
A. It is politically engaged.
B. It privileges text over context.
C. It has a symbiotic relationship with Formalism.
D. It studies the means of production of a text.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Cultural Studies is an explicitly politically engaged discipline examining power, ideology, and hegemony (A), and it investigates the material and institutional means of cultural production and reception (D) rather than privileging isolated formalist texts.

items.title: Mock #13 · Q4
items.stem: Which of the following information has now been excluded while making an entry for a book in the 8th edition of MLA Handbook for Writers of Research Papers?
items.explanation: The MLA 8th edition dropped the place of publication from book entries, except in special cases.

items.title: Mock #13 · Q5
items.stem:
Arrange the following in the chronological order of their publications :
(A) Hemachandra Joshi's Plays for the Young
(B) Balwant Gargi's The Knife
(C) P. K. Bosu's Conrad and Leonora
(D) Abdul Ali's The Land of Twilight
(E) D. M. Borgaonkar's Image Breakers
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: The oldest of these Indian English plays is Abdul Ali's The Land of Twilight, followed by Bosu's Conrad and Leonora, then Gargi's The Knife, Joshi's Plays for the Young and finally Borgaonkar's Image Breakers. (Key doubtful: dates of some titles are hard to confirm.)

items.title: Mock #13 · Q6
items.stem:
Who among the following contemporaries of John Donne wrote the following lines on his
death : "Here lies a king, that ruled as he thought fit/The universal monarch of wit" ?
items.explanation: Thomas Carew concluded his famous tribute 'An Elegy upon the Death of the Dean of Paul's, Dr. John Donne' (published in the 1633 edition of Donne's Poems) with the epitaph: 'Here lies a King, that rul'd as he thought fit / The universal Monarchy of wit.'

items.title: Mock #13 · Q7
items.stem:
Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R
Assertion A: The implied reader shifts attention from the real reading individual to a disembodied dimension of reception,
intricately interwoven into the text.
Reason R: The 'Dear Reader,' invoked in the realist novels, is a fictional representation of the distant reader.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
A is correct but R is not correct
Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is not correct but R is correct
items.explanation: In Wolfgang Iser's reception theory (The Implied Reader, 1972), Assertion A accurately defines the implied reader as a textual structure of response, and Reason R is also true regarding the fictive 'Dear Reader' in realist novels, though R does not explain A.

items.title: Mock #13 · Q8
items.stem:
“Fair is my love, and cruel as she’s fair; Her brow-shades frown, although her eyes are sunny”.
The above lines are characterized by :
items.explanation: The line 'Fair is my love, and cruel as she's fair' (from Samuel Daniel's sonnet sequence Delia, 1592) employs antithesis, placing contrasting qualities (fairness and cruelty) in direct rhetorical opposition within the same poetic line.

items.title: Mock #13 · Q9
items.stem:
1. A content word is not a function word.
2. A content word has lesser meaning than a function word.
3. A content word has no function.
4. A content word bears lexical meaning whereas a function word just about means functionally.
Which of these statements are correct ?
items.explanation: In English grammar, content (lexical) words—nouns, main verbs, adjectives, and adverbs—are distinct from function words (1) and carry independent dictionary meaning, whereas function (grammatical) words—articles, prepositions, pronouns, and conjunctions—serve primarily to signal syntactic relationships (4).

items.title: Mock #13 · Q10
items.stem:
Why, all men strive and who succeeds ?"        These
lines are from
items.explanation: The lines 'Fail I alone, in words and deeds? / Why, all men strive and who succeeds?' occur in Robert Browning's dramatic monologue 'The Last Ride Together' (published in Men and Women, 1855), spoken by a rejected lover taking one final horseback ride with his beloved.

items.title: Mock #13 · Q11
items.stem:
Match List I with List II
List I
List II
(Novel)                                      (Writer)
A. A Handful of Dust
I. E. M. Forster
B. Brighton Rock
II. Evelyn Waugh
C. Howard's End
III. D. H. Lawrence
D. The Plumed Serpent
IV. Aldous Huxley
E. Those Barren Leaves
V. Graham Greene
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A- II; B-V; C-I; D-III; E-IV
A- I; B-IV; C-II; D-III; E-V
A- III; B-I; C-V; D-II; E-IV
A- V; B-II, C-IV, D-I; E-III
items.explanation: A Handful of Dust (1934) was written by Evelyn Waugh (A-II), Brighton Rock (1938) by Graham Greene (B-V), Howards End (1910) by E.M. Forster (C-I), The Plumed Serpent (1926) by D.H. Lawrence (D-III), and Those Barren Leaves (1925) by Aldous Huxley (E-IV).

items.title: Mock #13 · Q12
items.stem: The structural analysis of signs was practised by
items.explanation: French critic and semiotician Roland Barthes pioneered the structural analysis of cultural signs and sign systems (semiology), notably in Mythologies (1957), Elements of Semiology (1964), and 'Introduction to the Structural Analysis of Narratives' (1966).

items.title: Mock #13 · Q13
items.stem:
Semiotics originated mainly in the works of two theorists.  They are :
(a)
Charles Sanders Peirce
(b)
Mikhail Bakhtin
(c)
Ferdinand de Saussure
(d)
Valentin Voloshinov
The right combination according to the code is __________
items.explanation: Modern semiotics (the systematic study of signs) originated independently at the turn of the twentieth century in the philosophical 'semiotic' of American pragmatist Charles Sanders Peirce (a) and the structural 'semiology' of Swiss linguist Ferdinand de Saussure (c).

items.title: Mock #13 · Q14
items.stem:
'The parish of rich women, physical
decay, /

Yourself…'

What do these make of W.B. Yeats
in W.H. Auden's view ?
items.explanation: In Section II of W. H. Auden's elegy 'In Memory of W. B. Yeats' (1939), Auden addresses Yeats directly with the lines: 'You were silly like us; your gift survived it all: / The parish of rich women, physical decay, / Yourself. Mad Ireland hurt you into poetry.'

items.title: Mock #13 · Q15
items.stem: Arrange the following groups of English writers in chronological order
options: The University Wits The Metaphysical poets Transitional poets The Aesthetes The Georgians The High Modernists
The Metaphysical poets The High Modernists Transitional poets The Georgians The Aesthetes The University Wits
The High Modernists The Georgians The Aesthetes Transitional poets The Metaphysical poets The University Wits
The University Wits The Metaphysical poets The Aesthetes Transitional poets The Georgians The High Modernists
items.explanation: The correct chronological sequence of these literary groups is: the University Wits (late 1580s–1590s), the Metaphysical poets (early-to-mid 17th century), the Transitional poets (mid-to-late 18th century), the Aesthetes (1880s–1890s), the Georgians (1910s–1920s), and the High Modernists (1920s–1930s).

items.title: Mock #13 · Q16
items.stem: Who enunciated the idea of myth as depoliticised speech in bourgeois society ?
items.explanation: In his foundational theoretical essay 'Myth Today' (in Mythologies, 1957), French semiotician Roland Barthes defined modern bourgeois myth as 'depoliticized speech' that strips cultural signs of historical contingency and presents them as natural, innocent facts.

items.title: Mock #13 · Q17
items.stem:
Given below are two statements. One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion (A): In second language learning, in the same classroom setting, some students progress rapidly through the initial stages of learning a new language while others struggle making very slow progress.
Reason (R): Some learners never achieve native-like command of a second language.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the option given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct.
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct.
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
items.explanation: Both (A) and (R) are true observations in second-language acquisition, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A): differences in initial classroom progress are explained by individual learner variables such as language aptitude, motivation, and learning styles, rather than ultimate attainment of native-like proficiency.

items.title: Mock #13 · Q18
items.stem: Who among the following is not associated with Cultural Imperialism?
items.explanation: Stanley Fish is a prominent American reader-response theorist known for his concepts of the 'informed reader' and 'interpretive communities', whereas cultural materialists and cultural studies scholars like Jonathan Dollimore, Alan Sinfield, and Raymond Williams directly investigated cultural imperialism, hegemony, and political ideology.

items.title: Mock #13 · Q19
items.stem:
Identify the correctly matched pair of
translators and translations.
(I)
A. K.
Ramanujan
(a) The Ramayana
(II) Manmathanath
Dutt
(b) The Bhagavad
Gita

Chatterjee

Shiva

Chandra Dutt

Mahabharata

(I)

items.explanation: These translators match with their English translations as follows: A. K. Ramanujan translated Kannada Virasaiva vacanas in Speaking of Siva (1973, I-c); Manmatha Nath Dutt translated The Mahabharata (1895–1905, II-d); Mohini Chatterji translated The Bhagavad Gita (1887, III-b); and Romesh Chunder Dutt translated The Ramayana (1899, IV-a).

items.title: Mock #13 · Q20
items.stem: Robert Browning's "Rabbi Ben Ezra" is a defence of
items.explanation: Robert Browning's dramatic monologue 'Rabbi Ben Ezra' (published in Dramatis Personae, 1864) is a spirited defence of old age against youth, famously opening with the lines: 'Grow old along with me! / The best is yet to be, / The last of life, for which the first was made.'

items.title: Mock #13 · Q21
items.stem:
Match List I with List II
List I
List II
(Book)                                      (Author)
A. English, August
I. Shyam Selvadurai
B. In Custody
II. Anita Desai
C. Such a Long Journey
III. Rohinton Mistry
D. Funny Boy
IV. Upamanyu Chatterjee
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A - III, B - II, C - I, D - IV
A - IV, B - II, C - III, D - I
A - I, B - II, C - IV, D - III
A - II, B - IV, C - I, D - III
items.explanation: English, August (1988) was written by Upamanyu Chatterjee (A-IV), In Custody (1984) by Anita Desai (B-II), Such a Long Journey (1991) by Rohinton Mistry (C-III), and Funny Boy (1994) by Shyam Selvadurai (D-I).

items.title: Mock #13 · Q22
items.stem: Who among the following considers a text as a "site of struggle between authority and popular culture"?
items.explanation: Russian theorist Mikhail Bakhtin, in Rabelais and His World (1965) and The Dialogic Imagination, theorized the novel and carnivalesque folk humor as a dialogic site of struggle between official monologic authority and popular culture.

items.title: Mock #13 · Q23
items.stem:
Which poems have NOT been composed by Adrienne Rich?

A. ‘Driving into the Wreck’
B. ‘Transcendental Etude’
C. ‘Snapshots of a Daughter-in-Law’
D. ‘The Applicant’
E. ‘Ripples on the Surface’

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: 'The Applicant' is a famous poem by Sylvia Plath (published in Ariel, 1965), and 'Ripples on the Surface' is a poem by A. R. Ammons, while 'Driving into the Wreck', 'Transcendental Etude', and 'Snapshots of a Daughter-in-Law' are by Adrienne Rich.

items.title: Mock #13 · Q24
items.stem: Who among the following observed that “Nothing can please many, and please long, but just representations of general nature”?
items.explanation: This famous maxim is stated by Samuel Johnson in his Preface to Shakespeare (1765), where Johnson argues that literature endures across centuries only when it faithfully mirrors universal human nature and general truth rather than transient local customs.

items.title: Mock #13 · Q25
items.stem:
Choose the right chronological sequence of the following books:
 A. Arundhati Roy, The God of Small Things
 B. Kiran Desai, The Inheritance of Loss
 C. Shashi Deshpande, That Long Silence
 D.  Jhumpa Lahiri, The Namesake
 Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: These Indian English novels were published in the chronological order: Shashi Deshpande's That Long Silence (1988, C), Arundhati Roy's The God of Small Things (1997, A), Jhumpa Lahiri's The Namesake (2003, D), and Kiran Desai's The Inheritance of Loss (2006, B).

items.title: Mock #13 · Q26
items.stem:
"So the baby was carried in a small deal box, under an ancient woman's shawl, to the churchyard that night, and buried by lantern-light, at the cost of a shilling, and a pint of beer to the sexton, in that shabby corner of God's allotment where He lets the nettles grow, and where all unbaptized infants, notorious drunkards, suicides and others of the conjecturally damned are laid."
From which novel is this excerpt taken?
options: Mill on the Floss by George Eliot
items.explanation: This passage occurs at the end of Phase the Second (Chapter XIV) of Thomas Hardy's Tess of the d'Urbervilles (1891), describing the midnight burial of Tess's illegitimate infant son, Sorrow, after the local parson refuses him a Christian burial.

items.title: Mock #13 · Q27
items.stem:
Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : Chaucer describes 'Madame Eglentyne' thus : 'She was so charitable and so pitous, She wolde wepe, if that she sawe a mous caught in a trappe'
Reason (R) : On her 'broche of gold full shene' was written Amor Vincit Omnia.
In the context of the two statements, which one of the following is correct ?
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
items.explanation: In the 'General Prologue' to The Canterbury Tales, both statements accurately describe Chaucer's Prioress, Madame Eglentyne—she weeps over a trapped mouse and wears a golden brooch inscribed with Amor vincit omnia ('Love conquers all')—but the brooch's motto does not explain her sentimental sympathy for animals.

items.title: Mock #13 · Q28
items.stem: Which among the following recent novels is a retelling of Sophocles's Antigone ?
items.explanation: Kamila Shamsie's novel Home Fire (2017), which won the Women's Prize for Fiction, is a contemporary reimagining of Sophocles's tragedy Antigone centred on a British Muslim family torn between state law and familial loyalty.

items.title: Mock #13 · Q29
items.stem:
Which of the following are books by Noam Chomsky?
A. Syntactic Structures
B. Verbal Learning and Verbal Behavior
C. Language and Society
D. Aspects of the Theory of Syntax
E. The Pragmatics of Politeness
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Syntactic Structures (1957, A) and Aspects of the Theory of Syntax (1965, D) are foundational linguistics monographs by Noam Chomsky, whereas The Pragmatics of Politeness (2014) was written by Geoffrey Leech.

items.title: Mock #13 · Q30
items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a quest narrative ?
items.explanation: Samuel Taylor Coleridge's unfinished Gothic poem Christabel (1797–1800) is a supernatural tale of demonic seduction set at Sir Leoline's castle rather than a journey or quest narrative, whereas Shelley's Alastor, Byron's Manfred, and Keats's Endymion all center on Romantic protagonists pursuing a metaphysical or ideal quest.

items.title: Mock #13 · Q31
items.stem:
Match List I with List II:
List I
(A) To the Lighthouse
(B) Sons and Lovers
(C) Finnegans Wake
(D) The Waste Land

List II
(I) 1913
(II) 1927
(III) 1939
(IV) 1922

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: D. H. Lawrence's Sons and Lovers was published in 1913 (B-I), T. S. Eliot's The Waste Land in 1922 (D-IV), Virginia Woolf's To the Lighthouse in 1927 (A-II), and James Joyce's Finnegans Wake in 1939 (C-III).

items.title: Mock #13 · Q32
items.stem: Identify the correctly matched set
options: The Shepheards Calender" - 1579 Tottels Miscellany - 1557 Astrophel and Stella - 1591 The Spanish Tragedie - about 1585
The Shepheards Calender" - 1559 Tottels Miscellany - 1579 Astrophel and Stella - 1585 The Spanish Tragedie - about 1591
The Shepheards Calender" - 1585 Tottels Miscellany - 1591 Astrophel and Stella - 1579 The Spanish Tragedie - about 1557
The Shepheards Calender" - 1579 Tottels Miscellany - 1591 Astrophel and Stella - about 1585 The Spanish Tragedie - about 1557
items.explanation: Richard Tottel's Songes and Sonettes (Tottel's Miscellany) was published in 1557, Edmund Spenser's The Shepheardes Calender in 1579, Thomas Kyd's The Spanish Tragedy was written around 1585–1587, and Philip Sidney's Astrophel and Stella was published in 1591.

items.title: Mock #13 · Q33
items.stem:
Which of the following works have NOT been authored by John Stuart Mill?
A. Subjection of Women
B. Thoughts on Parliamentary Reform
C. Past and Present
D. Explorations
E. On Liberty
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Past and Present (1843, C) was written by Thomas Carlyle and Explorations (1946, D) by Scrutiny critic L. C. Knights, whereas The Subjection of Women (1869, A), Thoughts on Parliamentary Reform (1859, B), and On Liberty (1859, E) were authored by John Stuart Mill.

items.title: Mock #13 · Q34
items.stem:
Who among the following Marxist
critics has reconsidered the classic
problem of 'base and superstructure"
in relation to literature ?
items.explanation: British Marxist critic Raymond Williams reconsidered the orthodox Marxist model of economic base and cultural superstructure in his influential 1973 essay 'Base and Superstructure in Marxist Cultural Theory' and in Marxism and Literature (1977).

items.title: Mock #13 · Q35
items.stem:
Which of the following is the correct sequence of stages in empirical research?
(A) Data Collection
(B) Hypothesis
(C) Validation
(D) Findings
(E) Analysis
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
items.explanation: Research starts with a hypothesis, then data collection, analysis, validation and finally the findings.

items.title: Mock #13 · Q36
items.stem: Erziehungsroman is a term which signifies:
items.explanation: *Erziehungsroman* is a German literary term meaning 'novel of education' or 'novel of upbringing', derived from *Erziehung* (education or training). It describes a narrative centered on the pedagogical, moral, and intellectual development of a protagonist, functioning as a specialized category of the Bildungsroman.

items.title: Mock #13 · Q37
items.stem:
Read the following statement and the reason given for it. Choose the right response.
Assertion (A) : Dickens's novels are called 'Newgate Novels'.
Reason (R) : They are called so, because Dickens adulates in these novels the careers and adventures of criminals.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation.
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation.
items.explanation: While Dickens's early crime fiction such as Oliver Twist (1837–1838) was grouped with the 1830s 'Newgate school' of fiction dealing with London criminals, Dickens explicitly refused to glamorize or adulate criminal life, portraying its grim squalor and moral consequences instead (making Reason R false).

items.title: Mock #13 · Q38
items.stem: Kipling's "The White Man's Burden" is addressed to
options: The British Imperial presence in Nigeria
The Belgian colonial expansion in the Congo
The American imperial mission in the Philippines
The British colonial entry into Afghanistan
items.explanation: Published in February 1899 with the subtitle 'The United States and the Philippine Islands,' Rudyard Kipling's poem 'The White Man's Burden' was directly addressed to the United States to urge American imperial annexation of the Philippines after the Spanish-American War.

items.title: Mock #13 · Q39
items.stem:
Which of the following statements are true about A. K. Ramanujan?
A. He is a poet of the sixties.
B. His poetry draws his sustenance from his awareness of Hindu heritage.
C. He has poor sense of rhythm.
D. His verse poorly utilises Akam constructed techniques.
E. He utilises Akam constructed techniques in his poetry.
items.explanation: Statements A, B, and E are true: A. K. Ramanujan emerged as a leading poet of the 1960s with The Striders (1966), drew rich thematic sustenance from his South Indian Hindu heritage, and skillfully integrated the interiorized conventions of classical Tamil akam poetry into his modern English verse. Statements C and D are false because Ramanujan is universally praised for his subtle, disciplined rhythmic craftsmanship.

items.title: Mock #13 · Q40
items.stem:
In one of her novels, Margaret
Atwood demonstrated the potentially
'Cannibalistic' nature of human
relationships. Identify the novel
items.explanation: In Margaret Atwood's debut novel The Edible Woman (1969), protagonist Marian MacAlpin's growing sense that her controlling fiancé Peter and consumerist society are devouring her identity causes her body to reject food, culminating in her baking a cake shaped like a woman for him to eat.

items.title: Mock #13 · Q41
items.stem:
Match the LIST-I with LIST-II
LIST-I | LIST-II
A. Francis Bacon | I. "Of Marriage"
B. Thomas Fuller | II. "Of Solitude"
C. Abraham Cowley | III. "An Essay on Death"
D. Sir Thomas Browne | IV. "Of Toleration"
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Francis Bacon is matched with 'An Essay on Death' (A-III), Thomas Fuller with 'Of Marriage' from The Holy State and the Profane State (B-I), Abraham Cowley with 'Of Solitude' from Several Discourses by Way of Essays (C-II), and Sir Thomas Browne with 'Of Toleration' (D-IV).

items.title: Mock #13 · Q42
items.stem:
Who made this following statement ?
“Truly neither philosopher nor historiographer could have entered into the gates of popular judgments, if they had not taken a great passport of poetry”.
items.explanation: Sir Philip Sidney wrote this line in An Apology for Poetry (published 1595), arguing that poetry serves as the first light-giver to knowledge and that philosophers and historians historically entered popular consciousness through the engaging power of verse.

items.title: Mock #13 · Q43
items.stem:
Which of the following statements are correct about voiced and voiceless sounds?
A. All 20 vowels sounds of English are voiced.
B. When the vocal cords move away from each other, the speech sounds articulated in this situation is called voiceless sounds.
C. The rapid opening and closing of the vocal cords is called the Vibration of the vocal cords and the sound produced in this vibration is called voiceless sound.
D. Fifteen out of twenty four consonants of English are voiced.
E. The articulatory system consists of a few organs in our leg and hand.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: In English phonetics (RP), all 20 vowel sounds are voiced (A), sounds produced when the vocal cords are drawn apart are voiceless (B), and 15 of the 24 English consonant phonemes are voiced while 9 are voiceless (D).

items.title: Mock #13 · Q44
items.stem: A critical question Eliot’s Prufrock poses, so important to an understanding of his character, is
items.explanation: In T.S. Eliot's "The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock" (1915), the timid speaker repeatedly obsesses over his existential hesitation with the pivotal question "Do I dare?", asking "Do I dare / Disturb the universe?" and "Do I dare to eat a peach?"

items.title: Mock #13 · Q45
items.stem:
Arrange the following Black American writers chronologically (in order of their birth)?
A. Maya Angelou
B. Toni Morrison
C. Alice Walker
D. Langston Hughes
E. James Baldwin
items.explanation: Langston Hughes was born in 1901, James Baldwin in 1924, Maya Angelou in 1928, Toni Morrison in 1931, and Alice Walker in 1944. Arranging these African American writers by their birth years yields the chronological order D-E-A-B-C.

items.title: Mock #13 · Q46
items.stem:
Why does Jean Baudrillard adopt
Disneyland as his own sign ?
options: Disneyland is by far the most eminently noticeable cultural sign in the post modern world
Disneyland captures 'essences' and 'non-essences' of Reality more convincingly than other cultural venues
Disneyland is both 'appearance' and 'reality' in the post modern visual game of handy-dandy. J-30-12
Disneyland is an artefact that so obviously announces its own fictiveness that it would seem to imply some counter balancing reality
items.explanation: In Simulacra and Simulation (1981), French postmodern theorist Jean Baudrillard argues that Disneyland is staged as an overtly imaginary fantasy world in order to make us believe that the rest of America surrounding it is 'real', thereby masking the fact that all of contemporary society is hyperreal.

items.title: Mock #13 · Q47
items.stem:
Assertion (A) : In The Duchess of Malfi Ferdinand sets a whole group of mad men on the Duchess and they dance and sing in a crazy manner.
Reason (R) : His desire was to provide a strange entertainment to drive the Duchess mad.
In the context of the two statements, which one of the following is correct ?
items.explanation: In Act IV, Scene 2 of John Webster's Jacobean revenge tragedy The Duchess of Malfi (1614), Duke Ferdinand sends a masque of madmen from a lunatic asylum to sing and dance wildly around the imprisoned Duchess in order to torture her psychologically and drive her to madness (making both A and R correct).

items.title: Mock #13 · Q48
items.stem: What was the centre set up for studying culture at the University of Birmingham called?
items.explanation: Founded by Richard Hoggart in 1964 at the University of Birmingham and later directed by Stuart Hall, the pioneering research institute was named the Centre for Contemporary Cultural Studies (CCCS).

items.title: Mock #13 · Q49
items.meta: Unit X: Research Methods and Materials in English
items.stem:
Which of the following are correct according to the MLA Handbook, 9th edition?
A. One inch margin on all sides is compulsory in a research page.
B. Co-ordinating conjunctions are written in bold letters in the title of a research paper.
C. Slash is used between two nouns paired as opposites.
D. Hanging indent in the works cited entry is ½ inches
E. Subordinating conjunctions are not written in bold letters in the title of the research paper.
items.explanation: According to the MLA Handbook (9th edition), page margins must be exactly 1 inch on all four sides (A), a forward slash without spaces is used to join paired contrasting or alternative nouns (C), and entries in the Works Cited list must use a hanging indent of 0.5 inches (½ inch) (D). Statements B and E are incorrect because paper titles in MLA style are never formatted in bold font.

items.title: Mock #13 · Q50
items.stem: Which of these Greek plays was a source for The Winter’s Tale ?
items.explanation: Shakespeare's romance The Winter's Tale (1611) draws directly upon Euripides' tragicomedy Alcestis, where Queen Alcestis dies for her husband Admetus and is brought back from the underworld veiled by Heracles, paralleling the miraculous restoration of Hermione.

items.title: Mock #13 · Q51

(ii) Loyalties
(iii) In the Jungle of Cities
(iv) The Family Reunion

List – II (Authors)

(2) Bertolt Brecht
(3) T.S. Eliot
(4) George Bernard Shaw

Codes : (i) (ii) (iii) (iv)
items.explanation: Heartbreak House (1919) is by George Bernard Shaw (4), Loyalties (1922) by John Galsworthy (1), In the Jungle of Cities (1923) by Bertolt Brecht (2), and The Family Reunion (1939) by T.S. Eliot (3).

items.title: Mock #13 · Q52
items.stem:
Identify the character who is not part of the group of three protagonists in Girish Karnad's
Hayavadana
items.explanation: In Girish Karnad's play Hayavadana (1971), the central love triangle consists of the three protagonists Devadatta (the man of intellect), Kapila (the man of body), and Padmini. Gautama is not a character in the play.

items.title: Mock #13 · Q53
items.stem:
Who among the following are the recipients of the Nobel Prize in Literature?
A. Orhan Pamuk
B. Somerset Maugham
C. Harold Pinter
D. Margaret Atwood
E. Herta Muller
Choose the correct answer from the options given below
items.explanation: Turkish novelist Orhan Pamuk (A, 2006), British playwright Harold Pinter (C, 2005), and German-Romanian novelist Herta Muller (E, 2009) were awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature, whereas W. Somerset Maugham and Margaret Atwood have not received the prize; thus A, C, E only.

items.title: Mock #13 · Q54
items.stem: Which of the following second- language learners would most likely acquire the second language more easily ?
options: a high school student who has been enrolled in mandatory classes in the second language since elementary school
a visitor to a country where the second language is spoken; he interacts with hotel and restaurant personnel using the second language
a business person for whom fluency in the second language may lead to career advancement
an immigrant living in a country where the second language is spoken; he feels accepted by speakers of the second language
items.explanation: According to John Schumann's Acculturation Model and Stephen Krashen's Affective Filter Hypothesis in Second Language Acquisition, an immigrant living in the target-language country who feels socially accepted by native speakers experiences low social distance and a low affective filter, acquiring the language most easily.

items.title: Mock #13 · Q55
items.stem: Arrange the following in the chronological order of the date/year of publication: (A) Chitra Banerjee Divakaruni's The Mistress of Spices (B) Anand Giridhar Das's India Calling: An Intimate Portrait of a Nation's Remaking (C) V.S. Naipaul's India: A Wounded Civilisation (D) Bharati Mukherjee's Desirable Daughters (E) Salman Rushdie's Midnight's Children Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: The chronological sequence of publication is: V.S. Naipaul's India: A Wounded Civilization (1977), Salman Rushdie's Midnight's Children (1981), Chitra Banerjee Divakaruni's The Mistress of Spices (1997), Bharati Mukherjee's Desirable Daughters (2002), and Anand Giridharadas's India Calling (2011) [(C), (E), (A), (D), (B)].

items.title: Mock #13 · Q56
items.stem: The line “Drop drop, slow tears” is the example of :
items.explanation: 'Drop drop, slow tears' from Phineas Fletcher's hymn 'A Litany' contains consecutive heavily accented syllables. A metrical foot composed of two stressed syllables is a spondee.

items.title: Mock #13 · Q57
items.stem:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R

Assertion A: Marxism makes no claim to universality.

Reason R: Postmodernism jettisons totalizing frameworks.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is correct but R is not correct
Ais not correct but R is correct
items.explanation: Postmodernism famously defines itself through incredulity toward metanarratives and the rejection of totalizing frameworks (R is correct), while classical Marxism's universalizing historical materialism is rejected by postmodern thought (A is correct). However, postmodernism's rejection of grand narratives is not the explanatory cause of Marxism's theoretical claims, meaning R does not explain A.

items.title: Mock #13 · Q58
items.stem: What is practical criticism ?
options: The close analysis of poems without taking account of any external information
A movement which wished to make literary criticism more relevant
The close analysis of literary texts in such a way as to bring out their political meaning
items.explanation: Pioneered by I. A. Richards in Practical Criticism (1929), 'practical criticism' is the method of close textual analysis of poems 'on the page' in isolation from external biographical, historical, or authorship information.

items.title: Mock #13 · Q59
items.stem:
Which of the following works have been written by Thomas Carlyle?
A. Of Heroes and Hero-Worship
B. The French Revolution
C. Of Human Bondage
D. The Hour and the Man
E. Hudibras
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: On Heroes, Hero-Worship, and the Heroic in History (1841, A) and The French Revolution: A History (1837, B) were written by Victorian essayist and historian Thomas Carlyle. Of Human Bondage (1915) is by W. Somerset Maugham, The Hour and the Man (1841) is by Harriet Martineau, and Hudibras (1663–78) is by Samuel Butler.

items.title: Mock #13 · Q60
items.stem: Which of the following characters instruct Faustus in the dark arts?
items.explanation: Valdes and Cornelius, two friends skilled in magic, teach Faustus necromancy in Marlowe's play.

items.title: Mock #13 · Q62
items.stem: Which of the following writers remarked that “You are your best thing” ?
options: George Eliot in The Mill on the Floss
Arundhati Roy in The God of small things
items.explanation: This comforting declaration is spoken by Paul D to Sethe in the poignant closing chapter of Toni Morrison's Pulitzer Prize-winning novel Beloved (1987), reassuring her of her own intrinsic self-worth: "You your best thing, Sethe. You are."

items.explanation: Late-Victorian naturalist novelist George Gissing wrote New Grub Street (1891, A) and The Odd Women (1893, C), whereas Agnes Grey (1847) was written by Anne Brontë and Mary Barton (1848) by Elizabeth Gaskell.

items.explanation: The famous 'Seven Ages of Man' monologue beginning 'All the world's a stage, / And all the men and women merely players' is spoken by the melancholy nobleman Jaques in Act II, Scene 7 of Shakespeare's pastoral comedy As You Like It.

items.title: Mock #13 · Q67
items.stem:
The concept of "eugenics" finds its illustration predominantly in the writings of
A. John Osborne
B. George Bernard Shaw
C. Eugene O'Neill
D. Harold Pinter
E. Arthur Miller

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Ideas of selective breeding and eugenics figure prominently in George Bernard Shaw's Man and Superman (1903) and Back to Methuselah (1921, B) as well as Eugene O'Neill's Strange Interlude (1928, C), corresponding to Option 3 (B and C only).

items.title: Mock #13 · Q68
items.stem:
Which Victorian poet is the author of the following lines ?
"God himself is the best Poet,
And the Real is His song."
items.explanation: These lines are from Elizabeth Barrett Browning's poem 'The Dead Pan' (1844), in which she rejects nostalgic paganism in favour of Christian truth and poetic realism, declaring in stanza 36 that 'God himself is the best Poet, / And the Real is His song.'

(D) A Literature of their Own
(I) Norman Holland
(II) Harold Bloom
(IlI) Maud Bodkin
(IV) Elaine Showalter
items.explanation: Maud Bodkin published Archetypal Patterns in Poetry (1934, A-III); Norman Holland wrote The Dynamics of Literary Response (1968, B-I) applying psychoanalysis to reader response; Harold Bloom formulated The Anxiety of Influence (1973, C-II); and Elaine Showalter published A Literature of Their Own (1977, D-IV).

items.title: Mock #13 · Q70
items.stem: Feste is a clown in
items.explanation: Feste (also called Lavatch's counterpart in Illyria) is the witty, musical court jester and fool in Olivia's household in William Shakespeare's romantic comedy Twelfth Night (c. 1601).

items.title: Mock #13 · Q71
items.stem:
In An Essay on Criticism, Pope
A. analyses the causes of faulty criticism and praises the great critics of the past.
B. analyses the causes of faulty criticism and characterises the good critic
C. analyses the structure of a good essay and praises the great critics of the past.
D. analyses the structure of a good essay and suggest how such an essay could be converted into good criticism.
E. analyses the merits of the poetry of Wordsworth and praises the great critics of the past.
Which of the above statements are correct?
items.explanation: In An Essay on Criticism (1711), Alexander Pope analyzes the causes of faulty criticism (such as pride, imperfect learning, and pedantry in Part II), characterizes the qualities of the ideal critic, and praises the great critics of antiquity and the Renaissance in Part III (A and B).

items.title: Mock #13 · Q72
items.stem: Which of the following statements on the ogarth press is FALSE ?
options: The ogarth press was founded in 1917 by Leonard and Virginia Woolf
The press was solely devoted to publishing international classics in translation
Its location was their home, called ogarth ouse
The press published translations of Gorky, Chekhov, Tolstoy, Dostoevsky, Rilke, Svevo and others
items.explanation: The Hogarth Press, established by Leonard and Virginia Woolf at Hogarth House in Richmond in 1917, was an eclectic modernist press that championed experimental original British writing (including Woolf's own novels and T. S. Eliot's The Waste Land), not solely translated works.

items.title: Mock #13 · Q74
items.stem:
In the following list, all seven events happened during one year :

2. Arthur Quiller-Couch publishes The Oxford Book of English Verse.
3. Pablo Picasso arrives in Paris.
4. Max Planck presents the Quantum Theory.
5. Hugo de Vries hits upon the concept of 'genes'.
6. Sigmund Freud publishes The Interpretation of Dreams.

items.title: Mock #13 · Q75
items.stem:
What are the points of convergence between Derrida and Barthes?
A. Both believe in the endless play in language and literary texts.
B. Both conclude that the meaning of a text is not final.
C. Both construe that language has retrospective power.
D. They believe that no meaning is reliable.
E. They believe that "the relationship between words, meanings and texts are intrinsic to meaning rather than the word itself."

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A, B, C and D only
A, B, D and E only
items.explanation: Poststructuralist theorists Jacques Derrida and Roland Barthes converge in affirming the endless play of signifiers in texts (A), the non-finality of textual meaning (B), the instability of fixed meaning (D), and the relational nature of signification across words and texts (E).

items.title: Mock #13 · Q80
items.stem: Which one of the following is false about V. S. Naipaul?
options: He won the Booker Prize for his novel A House for Mr. Biswas.

items.title: Mock #13 · Q82
items.stem: Who among the following invented 'inscape' and 'instress'?
items.explanation: Victorian poet Gerard Manley Hopkins coined the terms 'inscape' (the unique, individualizing design or inner essence of a natural thing) and 'instress' (the divine energy that sustains an inscape and transmits it to the perceiver).

options: Renunciation of historical responsibility and commitment
items.explanation: Following Albert Camus's publication of The Rebel (L'Homme révolté, 1951), Jean-Paul Sartre and the editorial board of Les Temps Modernes criticized Camus for abandoning historical engagement and revolutionary political commitment in favor of an abstract, detached moral stance.

items.explanation: The metrical feet match their prosodic definitions as follows: a Trochee is a stressed syllable followed by an unstressed syllable (A-III), a Dactyl is one stressed syllable followed by two unstressed syllables (B-II), a Spondee consists of two stressed syllables (C-I), and an Iamb is an unstressed syllable followed by a stressed syllable (D-IV).

items.explanation: Culture and Imperialism (1993) is the seminal postcolonial critique written by Edward Said, whereas Keywords (1976), Culture and Society (1958), and The Country and the City (1973) are seminal books by Raymond Williams.

items.title: Mock #13 · Q91
items.stem:
Read the following passage, and answer the question that follows: (91-95)

However, faced with this world of faithful and complicated objects, the child can only identify himself as owner, as user, never as creator; he does not invent the world, he uses it: there are, prepared for him, actions without adventure, without wonder, without joy. He is turned into a little stay-at-home householder who does not even have to invent the mainsprings of adult causality; they are supplied to him ready-made: he has only to help himself, he is never allowed to discover anything from start to finish. The merest set of blocks, provided it is not too refined, implies a very different learning of the world: then, the child does not in any way create meaningful objects, it matters little to him whether they have an adult name; the actions he performs are not those of a user but those of a demiurge. He creates forms which walk, which roll, he creates life, not property: objects now act by themselves, they are no longer an inert and complicated material in the palm of his hand.
— Roland Barthes, "Toys" (Excerpt from Mythologies)

The world of objects makes the child
items.explanation: In Roland Barthes's essay 'Toys' from Mythologies (1957), complicated adult-like toys reduce the child to a passive owner, user, or 'actant' who merely performs ready-made actions without adventure, wonder, or true creative invention.

He creates forms which walk, which roll, he creates life, not property: objects now act by themselves, they are no longer an inert and complicated material in the palm of his hand.
— Roland Barthes, "Toys" (Excerpt from Mythologies)

Which of the following is a correct interpretation?
options: The child claims the object as his property.
The objects that the child holds are obscure and useless.
In touching the object, the child creates dynamic forms of life.
The child cannot understand the design of the object.
items.explanation: When given simple building blocks rather than refined adult replicas, the child acts as a demiurge who creates dynamic forms that walk and roll, generating living action rather than static property.

items.title: Mock #13 · Q96
items.meta: Unit IV / Unit VIII: Prose & Criticism
items.stem:
Read the following poem, and answer the question that follows (96-100):

Mr Bleaney

'This was Mr Bleaney's room. He stayed
The whole time he was at the Bodies, till
They moved him.' Flowered curtains, thin and frayed,
Fall to within five inches of the sill,

Whose window shows a strip of building land,
Tussocky, littered. 'Mr Bleaney took
My bit of garden properly in hand.'
Bed, upright chair, sixty-watt bulb, no hook

Behind the door, no room for books or bags —
'I'll take it.' So it happens that I lie
Where Mr Bleaney lay, and stub my fags
On the same saucer-souvenir, and try

Stuffing my ears with cotton-wool, to drown
The jabbering set he egged her on to buy.
I know his habits — what time he came down,
His preference for sauce to gravy, why

He kept on plugging at the four aways —
Likewise their yearly frame: the Frinton folk
Who put him up for summer holidays,
And Christmas at his sister's house in Stoke.

But if he stood and watched the frigid wind
Tousling the clouds, lay on the fusty bed
Telling himself that this was home, and grinned,
And shivered, without shaking off the dread

That how we live measures our own nature,
And at his age having no more to show
Than one hired box should make him pretty sure
He warranted no better, I don't know.
— Philip Larkin

The poem, "Mr. Bleaney", is written in a __________ form.
items.explanation: Philip Larkin's 'Mr Bleaney' (written 1955, collected in The Whitsun Weddings, 1964) opens in a dramatic mode with the landlady's direct speech showing the room to a prospective lodger ('This was Mr Bleaney's room...') and the speaker's reply ('I'll take it').
